parsed.explanation: Combined regime is elevated risk: border discrepancy can trigger refusal and a possible lifetime fraud finding, federal facilities and custody policies impose birth-sex exposure, immigration custody abuse is documented, and minors face an upheld state care ban. Mitigating this, the state currently places no restroom restriction on gender-identity use, courts have enjoined several national orders, and a gender-identity hate-crime aggravator exists. No imprisonment or execution for trans presence alone is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: February 2025 cable: document discrepancy or reasonable doubt about sex instructs refusal and further evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation can support permanent lifetime ineligibility for fraud. X markers no longer processed; confiscations and strandings reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration. Fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and limited waivers exist. Civil-liberties suit over passport markers is pending.
entry_documents.interaction: State motor-vehicle marker ban from February 2026 mainly affects resident licences, but a visitor needing state identification faces mismatch. Border refusal is the operative traveller-facing exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody: transgender men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. National prisons from 2026 adopted short haircuts, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution described as conversion therapy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border discrepancy or arrest can lead to detention where birth-sex placement, care removal and reported abuse increase severity. Bureau stopped reporting transgender prisoner numbers from 2025.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity. State facility bill passed upper chamber 37-8 in January 2026 but received no lower-chamber hearing and is not law.
federal_state_facilities.protection: As of April 2026 state law places no restriction on restroom use matching gender identity; two cities protect use by ordinance. Proposals to criminalise have died in committee since 2021.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Protective state law does not cancel the national government-funded facility rule in federal buildings. State schools and universities remain exposed if the pending bill advances.

care_services.exposure: State law upheld in November 2024 bans surgery, puberty blockers and hormones for under-18s, with phase-out for existing patients. National orders and proposed rules restrict minor care and public insurance; justice department subpoenaed hospital records for patients under 19.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor cannot obtain banned care here and a parent obtaining it elsewhere may face records scrutiny. Adult care availability is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; December 2025 reward memorandum uses radical gender ideology twice. National order directs investigation of schools and criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states it will not target people who simply disagree. Several national orders have been blocked or enjoined in court.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises police-interest and outpatient/school encounter risk, even though it is not a standalone criterion for arrest rewards.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minor faces upheld state ban on transition procedures, national investigation and funding threats concerning school gender-ideology, and possible hospital-records subpoena. Resident school law requires parental notice on name, pronoun or title requests from non-emancipated minors.
minors_guardians.protection: Existing patients had a phase-out. In August 2023 a national appellate court upheld preliminary injunction barring schools limiting a transgender student bathroom use during litigation.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian is not the care-ban defendant, but provider liability can force denial, separation of care from the child, school inquiry or missed treatment during travel.

street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crimes law since April 2019 allows harsher sentences where gender identity motivates an offence, as an aggravating circumstance. National hate-crime statute also covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No state-specific trans violence rate, police response record or enforcement frequency for the aggravator is documented, so street risk cannot be treated as proven safe.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, challenges to January 2025 orders, proposed health rules and civil-liberties challenge to the state identification ban are unresolved. Exposure therefore depends on measures in effect at travel.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked or enjoined several orders, granted a preliminary bathroom injunction, and hate-crime enhancement provides potential recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Functioning courts mitigate some paper protections, but do not cancel documented border, federal facility or custody exposures already operating.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this case: documented birth-sex prison housing with frequent assaults, cross-dressing arrest and slow remedies. Here birth-sex custody and conversion practices are documented nationally, but state is not shown imposing that prison rule and no cross-dressing offence applies.

Similar to this case: routine border refusal and exclusion without imprisonment, weak remedies. This case is higher because state restroom use is currently lawful, courts have enjoined orders, and existing X documents remain valid, unlike a universal visitor register.

Lower than this case: extended secondary screening, hours of delay and discretionary refusal, with remedies slow but no credible detention. Here possible lifetime ineligibility, documented immigration-custody abuse and minor care bans raise severity beyond administrative friction.

Far lower than this case: explicit equality law, chosen-name documents, independent oversight and only isolated questioning. Here national policy rejects X markers, mandates birth-sex documents, restricts federal facilities and frames pro-transgender ideology as a counterterrorism priority.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is document discrepancy at entry leading to refusal or fraud scrutiny, then birth-sex federal facilities and, if detained, documented custody abuse and care removal. State restroom law and courts provide real mitigations, but the pending facility bill, resident identification ban, upheld minor care ban and national threat-framing keep the combined regime in elevated risk, especially for families.
